//: The MAUI workload set is pinned here and not in ../global.json, because a workloadVersion applies to every project under the file that carries it: with the pin one level up, an ordinary test project cannot build unless the pinned set resolves too. The pin is load-bearing -- without it the workload set floats to a MacCatalyst version that demands a newer Xcode than the one installed, so bump the two together. The set pinned here, 10.0.204, needs Xcode 26.3: an iOS or MacCatalyst build against an older one fails outright, so select it with DEVELOPER_DIR when several are installed. rollForward is latestPatch and must stay that way, measured rather than reasoned: setup-dotnet resolves ../global.json, whose latestPatch gets it the newest patch in the band -- 10.0.204 on the runners as of 2026-08-31 -- and that is the SDK whose baseline set the workload pin is matched against. The two track each other only because both are allowed to move. Setting disable here asks for exactly 10.0.201, which is not what any runner installs, and both platform jobs then fail in dotnet workload restore with 'A compatible .NET SDK was not found'. version is repeated from ../global.json rather than inherited -- global.json does not merge, the nearest file wins outright -- so a build started from this directory resolves the same way as one started from the repository. Keep both fields in sync with that file.
